provenance_rule: Rows are one of two things and say which. READ: the official document was fetched and read in full on 2026-11-17 - the Bellagio Friday/Saturday/Sunday structure sheets and the Caesars Palace 2026 daily NLH flyer. CITED, NOT RE-READ: the Wynn rows, which come from an earlier session's read of the WPT structure PDF. Nothing is taken from an aggregator, and a value that could not be confirmed on an official page was deleted rather than repeated - see HS-DAILY, whose start times an earlier session recorded and this pass removed because no official page carries them.

rows.name: $600 No-Limit Hold'em - Fridays 11:00 a.m.
rows.fee_split: $510 to Prize Pool; $50 House Fee; $40 Voluntary Staff Gratuity (rule 5).
rows.entry_rule: Players may buy-in and re-enter through the end of level 8 (Including Break). Tournament Surrender is allowed on Level 8 break (rule 3).
rows.reason: Re-entry is allowed through level 8, and a $40 'voluntary' staff gratuity buys an extra 15,000 starting chips on top of the base 15,000 - money buys both a second bullet and double the stack (rules 3, 6 and 7).
rows.chips: 30,000 (15,000 base + 15,000 from the optional paid gratuity)
rows.notes: Bellagio states it withholds nothing from the prize pool for gratuities and that the gratuity goes to staff - but the effect at the table is that $640 buys a 30,000 stack and $600 buys a 15,000 stack. No guarantee is stated anywhere on the sheet.

rows.name: $1,100 No-Limit Hold'em - Saturdays 11:00 a.m. (sheet also quotes a $600 buy-in)
rows.fee_split: CONTRADICTORY ON THE SHEET. The heading says 'NLH $1100 BUY-IN'; rule 7 says 'Of the $600 Buy-in, $510 goes to the Prize Pool, $50 is Admin Fees and $40 is optional staff gratuity.' Both figures cannot be right. The file name says $1000.
rows.entry_rule: Registration open until the start of level 10 (rule 3). Multi-flight: flights 1A, 1B, 1C and 1D, each playing down to the money (12.5%); a player must bag chips to reach the combined Day 2 (rule 6).
rows.reason: Multi-flight with open registration into level 10, so a bust can be re-bought into a later flight, and the optional $40 gratuity buys an extra 20,000 chips.
rows.chips: 40,000 (20,000 base + 20,000 from the optional paid gratuity)
rows.notes: The sheet is internally inconsistent about the buy-in (heading $1,100 vs rule 7 $600) and it names a specific past date - 'Combined Final Day 2 (9/13/26)' - so it was not written for the current season. Treat the buy-in and the guarantee as unconfirmed until Bellagio publishes a current sheet. See flag FG-09.

rows.name: $400 H.O.R.S.E. - Sundays 11:00 a.m.
rows.fee_split: $340 to Prize Pool; $35 House Fee; $25 Voluntary Staff Gratuity (rule 1).
rows.entry_rule: Players may buy-in and re-enter through the end of level 8 (Including Break). Tournament Surrender is allowed on Level 8 break (rule 5).
rows.reason: Re-entry through level 8, plus a $25 'voluntary' gratuity that buys an extra 15,000 starting chips - half the starting stack is for sale (rules 1, 2 and 3).
rows.chips: 30,000 (15,000 base + 15,000 from the optional paid gratuity)
rows.notes: Thirty-minute levels; game changes every 8 hands; pays approximately 12.5% of the field (rule 7). No guarantee is stated.

rows.name: Daily No-Limit Hold'em 10:00 - $100 buy-in, $1,000 GTD
rows.fee_split: Of the $100 buy in, $70 goes to the prize pool and $30 is held by Caesars Palace as a maintenance fee. Of the $50 add-on, $45 goes to the prize pool and $5 is held as a maintenance fee.
rows.entry_rule: Participants may re-enter, by paying the entry fee, upon elimination within the first break of play (Sign Up rule 3). Registration closes at the start of level seven. A $50 add-on for 15,000 chips may be taken at the first break only.
rows.reason: Re-entry is allowed after an early elimination and there is a $50 add-on for 15,000 chips, so more money buys both a second bullet and a bigger stack.
rows.notes: 20-minute levels, 10-minute break every six levels, sign-ups open one hour before the start, minimum six players or the tournament is cancelled and refunded.

rows.name: Daily No-Limit Hold'em (10:00 AM / 5:00 PM / 2:00 AM)
rows.fee_split: Not printed on the official page. The page does say the FIRST $20 add-on goes to dealer appreciation and the SECOND add-on goes to the prize pool.
rows.entry_rule: On-site registration and UNLIMITED RE-ENTRIES until the start of level 5 (approximately 11:15 a.m. for the 10 a.m. event, 6:15 p.m. for the 5 p.m. event, 3:15 a.m. for the 2 a.m. event). Add-on: 10,000 chips for $20, twice, at any time before the end of registration.
rows.reason: Unlimited re-entries until level 5 plus two paid add-ons - and the page states plainly that the first add-on does not even go into the prize pool.
rows.note: Buy-in is not printed on the official page, so it is left blank (not guessed).
rows.notes: Downtown, not on the Strip - a taxi or a long walk from every other venue here. 15% pay table. Must have a 24K Select Club card. The buy-in genuinely is not printed on the official page, so it stays blank.

rows.property: Horseshoe Las Vegas (Hall of Fame Poker Room)
rows.name: Daily No-Limit Hold'em tournaments
rows.reason: The only official Caesars source found is a marketing article that says Horseshoe runs a daily tournament slate; it publishes no times, buy-ins or rules. The start times carried here by an earlier session (9 AM / 11 AM / 2 PM / 5 PM / 8 PM / 11 PM) could not be confirmed on any official page, so they have been removed rather than repeated.
rows.notes: Ask the Hall of Fame Poker Room for its current daily flyer. Until then this row tells you only that daily tournaments exist, which is not enough to plan a day.

rows.name: $150 No-Limit Hold'em, $2,000 GTD (Saturday 11:10 AM) and $120 dailies (11:10 AM / 7:10 PM / 11:10 PM)
rows.date_range: recurring daily (schedule PDF titled 'August', year not printed)
rows.entry_rule: The official schedule PDF states no re-entry, rebuy or add-on rule for these events. It does state: 'Sunday through Friday - Players with 5 entries or more in $120 Daily Tournaments will receive one (1) free entry to the Saturday $150 NLH $2,000 Guarantee.'
rows.reason: Free entry earned by volume of paid entries, so a player who buys more $120 entries pays less per Saturday seat. The PDF says nothing about re-entry either way, so the daily events are not confirmed single-entry.
rows.note: Also flagged: PDF is labelled August with no year, and the PDF and web page disagree on the start time (FG-10).
rows.notes: Read 2026-11-17. The PDF is titled 'MGM Grand August Tournament Schedule' and prints no year, so it may not be the current schedule. It gives a Saturday start of 11:10am, which contradicts the 11:00 shown on MGM's web page (flag FG-10). The dailies are $120 with 25,000 chips and 15-minute levels; the Saturday event is $150 with 20-minute levels.

rows.name: $240 No-Limit Hold'em Rebuy & Add-on, $40K GTD (Friday, 12:00 PM)
rows.fee_split: $35 Tournament fee + $15 poker staff service charge + $190 prize pool = $240. From each $200 rebuy: $10 staff service charge and $5 tournament fee. From the $100 add-on: $5 staff service charge and $5 tournament fee (rule 3).
rows.entry_rule: UNLIMITED $200 REBUYS for 25,000 chips whenever a player is at 15,000 chips or fewer, plus one $100 add-on for 15,000 chips, all available until the start of level 9 (approximately 4:30 p.m.). RE-ENTRY IS NOT ALLOWED - rule 4. All rebuys must be made immediately from the player's original seat.
rows.reason: Unlimited rebuys and an add-on. Note the unusual wording: rebuys are allowed, re-entry after busting is not, so this is the one Wynn daily where you cannot buy a fresh bullet once eliminated - but you can keep buying chips while short.
rows.notes: The official sheet warns: 'The Tournament will be offered Friday and may be suspended during Seniors Events, Classic Events, or other Tournament Series.' The WPT World Championship runs at the same poker room 2026-11-27 to 2026-12-21, so this event may not run at all during your trip - call the room to confirm before planning a day around it.
